data.long_meaning: Dodiya is a name derived from the Sanskrit language. It is believed to be the name of the Goddess of Prosperity and Wealth. In Hindu mythology, she is often depicted as holding a lotus or a pot filled with gold coins. She is invoked for financial success and material abundance. The name Dodiya is also associated with the goddess Lakshmi, who is the deity of wealth and prosperity in Hinduism.

data.etymology: Dodiya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dodiya total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dodiya reflects the Hindu belief in the importance of material wealth and prosperity. It serves as a reminder of the Hindu Gods and Goddesses that oversee these aspects of life, and the role they play in granting success and abundance to their devotees. The use of this name in daily life can be seen as a way of connecting to these divine forces.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dodiya holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the Hindu goddess of wealth and prosperity. It is a reminder of the importance of invoking the blessings of the divine to attain material as well as spiritual success. The name also signifies the realization that wealth and prosperity are not only material possessions, but also a state of mind and an expression of divine grace. By calling upon the name Dodiya, one can connect with the divine energies of abundance and prosperity, and invite them into their life for their upliftment and growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dodiya is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Dodh' which means 'milk'. Symbolically, this name represents the purity and nourishment one receives from their parents and the divine. Spiritually, it signifies the inner joy and contentment attained through the pursuit of knowledge and devotion to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Dodiya Chiefs: A local dynasty ruled the region of Saurashtra from the 12th to the 15th centuries, with their capital at Dwarka. The Dodiya rulers were vassals of the Solanki kings, and their power peaked during the reign of Jayasimha Sanskriti (1241-1267 CE).

The Dodiya rulers were also known as the 'Lords of Dwarka'. They claimed descent from Lord Krishna and were considered to be protectors of the Hindu pilgrimage site of Dwarkadhish. Their power declined in the 15th century due to invasions by Muslim rulers.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Dodiya' has gained modern relevance in various contexts in India. In business circles, it is often associated with Dodiya Industries Limited, a leading manufacturer of engineering components. In legal proceedings, it is used as a surname, as in the case of Dodiya vs. Dodiya, a land dispute case heard in the High Court of Gujarat. In political discourse, 'Dodiya' is mentioned in reference to Dodiya Patel, a prominent community leader and elected representative in the Rajya Sabha.
